summary: Charles Edmund Godakumbura (1907–1977) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kingswood College. He served as a Senior Lecturer at the University of London from circa 1953 to 1959.

Charles Elliott (1776–1856) was an Indologist who worked for the East India Company from circa 1795 to 1814. He later served as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1836 to 1856.

Charles Gabriel Seligman (1873–1940) was an Indology scholar who studied at St Thomas' Hospital from circa 1892 to 1896. He held a post at the University of London from circa 1910 to 1934 and taught Bronislaw Malinowski.

Charles Goodman is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Allan Gibbard in 2002. He was attested as an Associate Professor at Binghamton University in 2013.

Charles H. Long (1926–2020) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1948–1962). He held posts at UNC Chapel Hill, Syracuse University, the University of Chicago, and UC Santa Barbara.

Charles Hallisey is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago, Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Charles Henry Tawney (1837–1922) was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as Chair of History and Principal at Presidency University, Kolkata, and later worked as Librarian of the India Office and India Office Library.

Charles Malamoud (born 1929) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris from circa 1948 to 1954. He taught at the University of Lyon (~1963–1979) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–1998).

Charles Philip Brown (1798–1884) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Haileybury. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1854) and later worked as Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1865–1884).

Charles Ramble is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who studied at Durham University and under Michael Aris. He held positions at Tribhuvan University, Wolfson College, the University of Oxford, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Charles Rieu (1820–1902) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Geneva and Bonn under Christian Lassen. He served as Curator of Oriental Manuscripts at the British Museum and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

Charles Rockwell Lanman (1850–1941) was an Indologist who studied at Yale and under William Dwight Whitney and Rudolf von Roth. He taught at Johns Hopkins (~1876–1880) and held professorships at Harvard University beginning in 1880.

Charles S. Prebish is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as Professor at Pennsylvania State University (~1972–2007) and held posts at Calgary and Utah State.

Charles Wei-hsun Fu (1933–1996) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at National Taiwan University and the University of Illinois System. He held a faculty post at Ohio University from circa 1969 to 1972.

Charles Wilkins (1749–1836) was an Indologist and founding member of the Asiatic Society. He held posts as Oriental Librarian for the East India Company (~1770–1836) and librarian for the India Office Library and Records (~1801–1836).

Charles de Harlez (1832–1899) was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as a Professor of Oriental Languages at KU Leuven from circa 1871 to 1899 and taught Louis de La Vallée Poussin.

Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche (1913–2015) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sera Khandro and Dorje Dradul, and his students included Keith Dowman and Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh (born 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities. She served as Professor of Philosophy at Thammasat University from circa 1969 to 2000.

Chen-kuo Lin is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his doctorate from Temple University. He served as a Professor and Distinguished Professor at National Chengchi University and held visiting positions at Leiden University and IIAS.

Cheng Yen (born 1937) is an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Yin Shun from circa 1963 to 2005. She founded the Buddhist Compassion Relief Tzu Chi Foundation.
